svg.title: Figure B-S1. One measurement window, in order of time
svg.desc: Schematic timeline of one measurement window, in four rows read top to bottom. Row 1: the scheduled start, the arm and GO. Row 2: the bracket reservation, a settle, the pre calibration with its screen, the reference corpus, the reference drift bound, and the start triplet of reference members with its spares. Row 3: the stages of science members, each preceded by a settle, with a midpoint reference between the decode workload and the prefill workload; one version for a single-model window and one for the contrast window. Row 4: the end triplet, the post calibration, the chain's exit, and the tail with the clock-step control. A bar under rows 2 to 4 shows the monitor and the whole-machine meter recording. An inset expands one stage into its settle, its members and the cooldowns between them. No measured data is shown.
svg.text: Figure B-S1. One measurement window, in order of time
Schematic of the registered design. Widths are not proportional to time. No measured data is shown.
1 The arm: the checks that decide whether the window's chain starts
the arm: six physical hazards are measured directly (Figure B-S3)
about 41 s of reads and probes, then the dwell:
a wait of 180 s to 2,700 s for a quiet machine
At GO the chain starts: the script that runs the stages of rows
2 to 4. That is about 4 to 47 minutes after the scheduled start.
From GO to the tail, the monitor and the whole-machine meter
2 Opening: the same in all three windows
Chain stops 1, 2, 3: the only points at which
the chain itself ends the window.
2 the pre calibration cannot be recorded
3 its pulse timing bound is above the pre
All three come before the first member.
3a Science stages of a single-model window (the 1.7B window and the 8B window): 100 science members, 119 members in all
A window runs row 3a or row 3b,
Quad: four members in the order
3b Science stages of the contrast window (side A the 1.7B model, side B the 8B model): 80 science members, 101 members in all
Inset: inside one stage of members
A member is one inference request run in its own
process: about 75 s of idle baseline, one warm-up, then
the measured request. The dashed bar between members
is the cooldown. It ends at the first 5 s idle reading that
is at most 2 times the previous member's idle baseline,
4 Closing and tail: the same in all three windows

g.data-label: chain's processes confirmed gone; members counted

svg.text: Once the final record is written, the harvest
Single-model window: 12 + 3 + (10 + 20 + 20) + 1 + (10 + 20 + 20) + 3 = 119 members. Contrast window: 12 + 3 + 20 + 1 + 20 + 1 + 20 + 1 + 20 + 3 = 101 members.
Either way: 1 settle before the pre calibration + 10 before stages of members = 11 settles of 60 s = 660 s.
order in time: left to right, then the next row
an instant: the scheduled start, GO, the chain's exit
the checks that decide whether the chain starts
a timing recording: 59 on/off pulses of a GPU load
a step in which no member runs
a 60 s sleep that lets the machine return to idle
one run of the fixed reference workload
runs, after one more settle, only if its stage lost a member
recorded, but not read by the reference drift check
members whose energies feed the reported numbers
a point at which the chain itself ends the window
a deliberate clock step, to test the clock check
the monitor and the whole-machine meter are recording
the request that the stages under it run
